title: Lesson 90: General systems architecture: building your own enterprise AI (capstone synthesis)
description: Tests the capstone build sequence: writing the eval set before the prompt, setting an acting identity instead of a shared integration identity, and the two levers that control input token cost.

questions.question: A team has a working warranty-assistant demo and wants to know what to produce before tuning prompt wording. What does the lesson say to write first?
options: A cost ceiling per interaction and per month
An AI inventory entry with a named owner and a review date
Write the eval set before the prompt
A tool permission matrix for the acting identity
questions.explanation: The first build step in the lesson is to write the eval set before the prompt, with expected outcomes and the source that settles each question, because a prompt without a scored set is a demo. The other artifacts matter as well, but every later trade-off is judged against the eval set, which is why it comes first.

questions.question: In a Review Board scenario, a candidate proposes that the assistant call case and entitlement APIs through one shared integration user with modify-all access. How does the lesson correct that design?
options: The agent acts as the user, not as a shared integration identity
The shared identity is acceptable if the tool calls are logged and audited monthly
The shared identity works provided the prompt instructs the model to filter records
The APIs should be replaced with a nightly batch synchronization job
questions.explanation: The lesson sets the identity before the tools and states that the agent acts as the user, not as a shared integration identity, so permission-aware retrieval comes from the identity the request runs under. Prompt instructions are not a security control, and auditing after the fact does not undo a disclosure that permission-aware retrieval would have prevented.

questions.question: A distributor's monthly inference invoice lands well above forecast at flat usage. Which two levers does the lesson identify for moving the input cost?
options: Retire the capability and rebuild it on a smaller hosted model
Move the retrieval index into the ERP to reduce token volume
Raise the per-user daily interaction cap so fewer people share accounts
Cache the stable part of the prompt, and cap retrieval at the top few passages
questions.explanation: The lesson names two engineering levers that move the input number: cache the stable part of the prompt, and cap retrieval at the top few passages instead of stuffing a manual chapter into every request. It shows the effect with a 45 percent cut in effective input cost, moving the monthly figure from 1,315 dollars to about 753 dollars at the same volume.
